advisers.message:
Dear [Adviser Name],

You have been invited to join ARCHIVIO — the Web-Based Digital Research Archive Management System of Southwestern University PHINMA.

As a Research Adviser, you will be able to:
• Manage your assigned student research groups
• Review and evaluate submitted manuscripts
• Track submission requirements and completion status
• Approve and forward papers to the Dean for publication

Please click the button below to activate your account and set up your credentials.

submissions.abstract: Traditional manual and unorganized digital archiving methods present significant challenges for undergraduate students and research advisers in locating, retrieving, and managing capstone research manuscripts, thereby hindering overall academic research efficiency. To address these challenges, this study developed and evaluated a web-based digital archiving system using an Agile software development methodology. Employing a mixed-methods research design, data were collected from students and research advisers through open-ended and closed-ended surveys, alongside document analysis. Quantitative data were analyzed using percentage distribution and weighted means, while qualitative feedback was interpreted through thematic mapping and word clouds. The baseline assessment highlighted widespread difficulties in manuscript retrieval and current storage practices. In response, the developed system integrated advanced modules including role-based dashboards for deans and advisers, content management tools, a publish queue, and requirements tracking. The evaluation of the proposed platform demonstrated a high level of acceptability among users, proving that the digital repository successfully streamlines manuscript submission, tracking, and discovery. This study concludes that the web-based digital archiving system offers an efficient, accessible, and organized solution for managing undergraduate student research, substantially improving institutional knowledge management and research accessibility.

suggestions.original: The evaluation of the proposed platform demonstrated a high level of acceptability among users, proving that the digital repository successfully streamlines manuscript submission, tracking, and discovery.
suggestions.reason: In academic writing, 'proving' is generally avoided unless dealing with strict mathematical proofs. Words like 'suggesting', 'demonstrating', or 'indicating' are preferred to maintain scientific objectivity.
suggestions.suggested: The evaluation of the proposed platform demonstrated a high level of acceptability among users, suggesting that the digital repository successfully streamlines manuscript submission, tracking, and discovery.

suggestions.original: Quantitative data were analyzed using percentage distribution and weighted means, while qualitative feedback was interpreted through thematic mapping and word clouds.
suggestions.suggested: Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including percentage distributions and weighted means, while qualitative feedback was analyzed using thematic analysis.
suggestions.reason: Grouping percentage distributions and weighted means under 'descriptive statistics' elevates the academic tone. Additionally, 'thematic analysis' is the formal methodology, whereas 'thematic mapping' and 'word clouds' are visual representations of that analysis.

aiScanResult.feedback: The abstract is exceptionally well-structured, clear, and maintains a highly professional academic tone. It perfectly follows the standard academic progression: background, problem statement, methodology, results, and conclusion. Grammar and syntax are strong, with only minor opportunities to temper strong claims (such as 'proving') and refine methodological terminology.
